chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Humran ibn Ayn, who said:

One of his family members wanted to get married but he could not find a compatible Muslim woman. So I mentioned that to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Where are you from the simple ones who do not know anything?'

key_terms.الْبُلْهِ: The simple/naive ones (referring to those lacking deep religious insight)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Wilayah in determining marital compatibility according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Humran ibn A'yan reports that a relative sought to marry but failed to find a suitable Muslim woman, prompting a consultation with Imam al-Sadiq (AS). The Imam’s rhetorical rebuke, 'Where are you from the foolish ones who know nothing?', critiques the narrow reliance on general Muslim identity while ignoring the critical Shia criterion of *Wilayah* (affiliation with the Ahl al-Bayt). This highlights the scholarly distinction between mere nominal Islam and the deeper theological compatibility required for marriage in Shia jurisprudence.
